answer.evidence: The seat is the main body. It is 14px wide from row 16 to row 25. A darker edge row at 16 is followed by lighter rows 17-18 and 20, and the lightest row at 21 acts as the front-edge line. Rows 22-24 step darker (L 151, 128, 103), which reads as the apron and eave shadow. Below that, legs run from rows 25 to 29 with a gap between them. That gives a seat top of about 6 rows and a front face of about 8 rows (apron plus legs). The backrest (rows 3-9, with slats at rows 12-13) is drawn face-on as a vertical panel, which is acceptable for a backrest. The silhouette is symmetric, with no receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate chair is a small single-tile-scale prop with only 7 distinct colours, against 14 for the bench and lamp and 38-40 for the stall and well. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark brown beside the wood, as in Beodeul, and it is not a sticker line. The wood ramp has about 3 steps (light slat, mid, dark), and the references use 5-6. The back slats and seat show little grain or per-plank highlight, so texture is only some. There are no flat fills of 5x5 or more. Because the piece is thin, I do not use the per-tile median against it. By eye it still looks a little thinner and flatter than the bench, which is the closest reference. It has fewer shading steps and fewer colours than a careful artist would accept next to the references, so it fails.
